Subject: Redwood demo — aligning schedules across teams

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the intro. We're excited to see Redwood in action. Our core stakeholders are in the US (East Coast), EMEA (UK/Germany), and a small APAC engineering presence in India and Japan. A few constraints on our side:

- EMEA folks prefer afternoons CET.
- APAC engineering will be partially OOO around Nov 29–Dec 1 (Diwali-related local leave for some India team members).
- US team has reduced availability on the week of Nov 30 because of regional coverage rotations and a US Thanksgiving carryover.

Can we aim for a slot in the window Nov 30–Dec 2 that gives reasonable overlap? Candidate times from our side:
- Nov 30, 09:00–10:00 ET (14:00–15:00 CET / 23:30–00:30 IST) — okay for US + EMEA, rough for India.
- Dec 1, 14:00–15:00 CET (05:00–06:00 PT / 18:30–19:30 IST) — favors EMEA/APAC overlap.

If those don't work, happy to run a quick poll. Also looping in Rajesh — he may want to ensure APAC edge cases are covered.

Best,
Claire

Hi Claire — thanks for the constraints and the two candidate slots.

Quick notes from our side:
- We see this scheduling friction a lot (DST shifts, regional leave windows). For short demos I usually recommend a rotating-window approach so the same persons aren't always stuck on late-night calls.
- I can do Nov 30 at 09:00 ET (your first option) but want to make sure a technical lead from APAC can join — if not, we should record the deep technical portion.

Proposed plan:
1) Run the demo on Nov 30 at 09:00 ET and record.
2) Schedule a follow-up technical deep-dive the next week at a slot that favors APAC (we can propose Dec 3 or 6).
3) I attached a simple proposed_time_grid.csv that maps candidate slots to participant overlap so we can pick the least-bad window.

Would you prefer I send a Doodle or a 3-option calendar poll?

Thanks,
Hannah

Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 07:22:00 -08:00
Subject: internal: rotating windows suggestion + DST note

Hannah / Lauren — quick internal note before we lock time with Claire.

- DST: US clocks just shifted in early November; Europe is on CET and will be stable through the end of November which makes a consistent mapping easier for the moment. That said, when we plan follow-ups in Q1 we should re-check DST boundaries (they differ in March/April).
- APAC: Japan Golden Week isn't until April, but India team has local festival leave windows that move each year (Diwali variable). For this near-term demo, the main issue is the India folks on Nov 29–Dec 1.

Suggestion: adopt a 2-step cadence for cross-region prospects like FinWise:
A) Surface-level exec/stakeholder demo that maximizes US/EMEA overlap (short, recorded).
B) Separate 60–90 minute engineering deep-dive scheduled on a rotating weekend/week evening favoring APAC attendance.

I've attached regional-slot-rotation-v1.csv — it shows 3-week rotation patterns so the same on-call person doesn't always take the 02:00 JST meeting. If you want, I'll convert that to a calendar series.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
